question: Many comparison rows share an alternative. Can reducing their influence during supervised training improve the actual protected portfolio without creating any inferred training labels?
source: Use the earlier autonomous portfolio's elected source member from its recorded training-only evidence. Change only that member's linear classifier. Use each fold's own genuinely fitted feature map, estimator and training rows. Reconstruct the original signed row augmentation and verify a uniform-weight refit reproduces the recorded primary probabilities within 0.000002. Require data-driven source election and a compatible signed logistic model; no fixed encoder name.
intervention: Give each training comparison inverse square-root weight by the number of training comparisons in its shared-text component. Normalize the mean weight to one, mirror weights with signed row augmentation and keep the original objective, regularization and random state. Other members and weights of the protected portfolio stay fixed. Compare retaining the original member, replacing half of its own contribution, and replacing all of its contribution.
gate: Nominate the best strictly positive share by internal primary accuracy; on ties prefer keeping or the smaller change. Freeze it before reading confirmation results. Stop on any confirmation loss. Require two nonnegative confirmations, at least one positive, and a pooled increase of at least 0.20 percentage points on the three disjoint held panels for a new independently reshuffled test. Report primary counts for every share, confirmation gains and actual fits. These are previously used training groups, not fresh external labels.
budget: One measured uniform control fit on primary and at most three weighted fits on the three panels. Exactly one receipt per actual classifier fit. No generative-model requests, external data or synthetic labels; course designated validation, formal test and H2 unopened.
